descriptionChirho: A male monarch or supreme ruler exercising royal authority over a people or territory; used both of earthly kings and of God or Christ as the ultimate King. Singular and plural forms across all cases represent the same lexical meaning with only grammatical inflection variation. Multilingual evidence: spa 'rey/reyes,' hin 'राजा/राजाओं,' arb 'مَلِكُ/المَلِكُ/مُلوكٍ,' kor '왕/왕들,' swa 'mfalme/wafalme.' The 115 occurrences span references to Herod (Matt 2:1), Jesus as King of the Jews (Matt 27:11, John 18:37), God as King (1 Tim 1:17, 6:15), the superlative 'King of kings' (1 Tim 6:15, Rev 17:14, 19:16), and various earthly monarchs throughout the Gospels, Acts, and Revelation.
